title: Partner entry slate & technical gates — marketplace listing draft
content:
Purpose
- Quick working slate that captures both copy variations and the pragmatic technical gates we need to accept a new partner listing into cloud marketplaces (AWS/GCP/Azure).
- This is not final copy — iterating with partners and legal. Use as the canonical draft for the launch sprint.

Audience
- Partner PM/engineering, partner success, marketplace program manager, legal/security reviewer, finance for SKU mapping.

High-level marketplace blurb variants (search/snippet friendly)
1) Short (30-50 chars):
- "Redwood Inference: predictable LLM inference"
- "Low-latency LLM serving for production apps"

2) Mid (70-120 chars — listing short description):
- Variant A (developer-first): "Run high-throughput, low-latency LLM inference with Redwood — hosted API, dedicated GPU pools, and private deployments for production-grade apps."
- Variant B (enterprise): "SLA-backed LLM inference with dedicated capacity, private VPC options, and cost controls for regulated workloads."

3) Long (detail for product page):
- "Redwood Inference delivers predictable, economical LLM serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Ship ML-powered features with built-in observability, model versioning, and cost-performance tooling — optimized for latency-sensitive and high-throughput production workloads."

Primary CTAs (pick one for marketplace storefront)
- "Get started — free credits"
- "Request demo & enterprise pricing"
- "Deploy in your VPC"

Benefit bullets (2–4 for listing card)
- "SLA-backed latency & uptime for critical LLM endpoints"
- "Dedicated GPU pools and autoscaling for predictable throughput"
- "Unified API across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments"
- "Cost controls: batching, caching, and quantization recommendations"

Taglines to A/B test in ads/featured slots
- "Bring LLMs to production — without building the stack"
- "Inference that scales: predictable latency, controllable cost"

Assets required (manifest for marketplace submission)
- 32px/64px/128px logos (SVG + PNG) — light & dark variants
- 1 hero screenshot (landed product UI or observability dashboard) 1920x1080
- 3 small screenshots (console views: routing, rollout, costs) 1280x720
- Architecture diagram (SVG + PNG) showing hosted/dedicated/private topologies
- 1–2 short customer quotes (permissioned) + logos (if available)
- Marketing copy: short, mid, long descriptions (this doc contains drafts)
- Pricing SKU matrix CSV (see billing section below)

Technical acceptance gates (must be completed before submission)
- [ ] Billing integration test (marketplace sandbox purchase flow verified end-to-end) — owner: Finance Eng / Billing
- [ ] Legal approval: marketplace terms + DPA check (redline acceptance) — owner: Legal
- [ ] Security posture summary doc: SOC2 status, penetration test summary, KMS/HSM support notes — owner: Security
- [ ] Deployment artifact: container/AMI image, or marketplace-specific manifest (ARM/x86 tags as required) — owner: Partner Eng
- [ ] Multi-region support matrix (which cloud regions we can serve from day 1) — owner: Infra
- [ ] Observable demo: a short runbook + sample metrics dashboard embedded in listing assets — owner: Observability
- [ ] Support routing: partner support contact + escalation policy for marketplace customers — owner: Customer Success

Minimum metadata for marketplace listing (fields on most portals)
- Company name: Redwood Inference
- Product name: Redwood Inference (Hosted & Dedicated)
- Category: AI / Machine Learning / Model Serving
- Pricing model: Usage-based + Reserved capacity (see SKU map)
- Contact: marketplace-sales@redwood.ai
- Data residency options: US, EU, APAC (per-region availability notes)

SKU & billing mapping (working table notes)
- Marketplaces expect discrete SKUs for: hosted API (token-based), dedicated reservations (monthly commit), private deployment license (annual fee), add-ons (observability retention).
- Action: create CSV with SKU, unit, price, billing term, mapping to internal meter id (billing eng to produce).
- Jira: GTMP-678 created for SKU upload and billing sandbox test.

Compliance and legal notes (quick, non-exhaustive)
- DPA: partner should confirm lawful basis for processing; include subprocessors list
- Export controls checklist: ensure no restricted model artifacts listed in assets
- Local law: if listing in EU marketplace, ensure representative contact & data processing clause visible
- Required docs often requested by marketplace: SOC2 Type II summary, HIPAA addendum if targeting health customers (optional), data encryption at rest & transit notes

Rollout plan (phases)
- Phase 0 (preflight, ~2 weeks): asset collection, billing integration, legal signoff, internal demo.
- Phase 1 (private listing, ~1 week): internal marketplace sandbox listing + test purchase path, invite 2–3 pilot customers.
- Phase 2 (public listing limited rollout, ~1 week): enable public listing in 1–2 regions, monitor purchases & support queue.
- Phase 3 (full launch, ~ongoing): add more regions, marketplace marketing assets live, monitor SLAs.

Launch risk register (short):
- Risk: Billing mapping mismatch leads to refunds. Mitigation: verify sandbox purchases and invoices before public listing.
- Risk: Security docs incomplete -> marketplace rejection. Mitigation: pre-submit SOC2 summary; schedule pentest report embargo.
- Risk: Regions not available -> customers see errors. Mitigation: disable region selection in listing until verified.

Open questions / decisions to make
- Which CTA is primary for free-tier vs enterprise? (Product/Marketing)
- Do we use marketplace-managed billing for reserved capacity, or route to contract sales? (Finance + Sales)
- Should we include an embedded live demo or just screenshots? (DevX + Legal for data exposure)

Quick timeline & owners (next 3 sprints)
- Sprint 1 (2 weeks): gather assets, billing CSV, legal DPA draft — owner: Maya / Finance / Legal
- Sprint 2 (2 weeks): integration test in marketplace sandbox, upload assets, internal QA — owner: Eng + Observability
- Sprint 3 (2 weeks): pilot customers invited, gather feedback, finalize copy — owner: Partner Success + Marketing

Slack / links / signposts
- Slack channel: #marketplace-launch (use for fast questions)
- Confluence: GTMP/marketplace-onboarding-2024 (linked)
- Jira epic: GTMP-600 (parent epic for rollout)

Notes & scratch (informal, keep)
- copy note: try reducing technical jargon in short descriptions — marketplace discovery favors plain language
- screenshot idea: short video gif of latency dashboard + cost breakdown might boost conversion in featured spot (confirm allowed file types)
- TODO: ask SRE if we can guarantee 99.95% across dedicated pool in the C-level marketing blurb — if not, reword to "SLA-backed tiers available"

Action items (immediate)
- [ ] Maya: create SKU CSV template and drop in this folder by EOD Fri (2024-11-22)
- [ ] Liam: schedule billing sandbox run and attach logs to GTMP-678
- [ ] Priya: draft legal redlines for marketplace terms and return to partner PM
- [ ] James: generate light/dark logo set + hero screenshot exports
- [ ] Sofia: draft two A/B email subject lines to use when we invite pilots

End of draft — please comment inline. Treat this as the living source of truth for marketplace copy + acceptance gates until we lock assets for submission.

References: links above + marketplace docs (AWS GovCloud requirements, GCP Marketplace procurement notes).
